title: Data graphs: pie charts and line graphs
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can read a pie chart as fractions of a whole, finding 1/2 for apples and 1/4 each for bananas and grapes.
The class can compare two bars by reading their heights and subtracting, and can read values and trends from a line graph.

modelAnswers.question: In a survey of 24 children, 13 chose soccer and 8 chose badminton. How many more chose soccer than badminton? Show the working.
Soccer got 13 votes and badminton got 8 votes. How many more votes did soccer get? Show the working.

commonErrors.misconception: A steeper line always means a bigger increase.
commonErrors.example: A learner draws the conclusion on the worksheet that graph A had the bigger increase because its line is steeper, without checking the axis scales.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: check both axes first - what are the two axis ranges, and by how much did each graph rise?
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: graph A runs 0 to 50 and graph B runs 0 to 200, and both sales rose by 20, so the increase is the same.

commonErrors.misconception: A steeper line always means a bigger increase.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner defends the steeper drawing by saying graph A rose by more than graph B.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say what decides how steep a line looks - then compare the rises from 20 to 40 on both graphs.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: slope depends on the axis scale, so two graphs can have the same rise of +20 but look different.

nextSteps: Reteach the axis-scale check, landing that steepness is judged against the axis scale before any slope comparison.
Practise reading both bar heights from the labels first before subtracting to compare them.
